skills.name: aid-learn-history

skills.name: aid-learn-reference

skills.name: aid-make
skills.description: The Make loop, which turns what a PRD describes into verified, reviewed changes. It opens with a breakdown into a task graph, cycles Delegate, Build, Verify over the ready tasks, reviews at the completion gates, and closes with a rebuild of the history. Use it when asked to build, implement, or fix something a PRD describes, to resume Make work in progress, or to dispatch implementation to the aid-* specialist roster.

skills.name: aid-make-breakdown
skills.description: The Breakdown stage of the Make loop, loaded by aid-make and not an entry point. Maps the path from the current code to what the PRD describes, in three steps: the gap, a strategy the user chooses, and a plan whose every step ends in a measurable result. The user reviews it as text; the orchestrator then builds the task graph from it, task by task.

skills.name: aid-make-build
skills.description: The Build stage of the Make loop, loaded by aid-make and not an entry point. The builder works inside the brief's scope and footprint, stops and reports on any mismatch between the brief, the PRD, and reality instead of improvising, and proposes PRD fragments for inconsistencies it finds.

skills.name: aid-make-delegate
skills.description: The Delegate stage of the Make loop, loaded by aid-make and not an entry point. Picks ready tasks from the task graph, claims them, and routes each to the cheapest aid-* role or project agent that can succeed, with a complete brief. Independent tasks go out in parallel.

skills.name: aid-make-rebuild
skills.description: The Rebuild stage of the Make loop, loaded by aid-make and not an entry point. Once the changes are complete and the state record is closed, it squashes the iteration history into a presentable, feature-by-feature series of commits on a new branch for whoever reviews the PR or merge, drops the working state, and proves the final tree matches.

skills.name: aid-make-review
skills.description: The Review stage of the Make loop, loaded by aid-make and not an entry point. Runs intent-isolated review lenses (PRD compliance, goal drift, quality, fresh eyes, plus project reviewer agents) at the completion gates, re-runs every task's checks as one batch, and gives every finding an outcome. Use the timing rules to decide when a review is due.

skills.name: aid-make-verify
skills.description: The Verify stage of the Make loop, loaded by aid-make and not an entry point. Proves a task with captured evidence: while iterating it validates only what the change needs, and a task is marked done only when the task tool has run its checks and they pass. Covers proving new tests can fail and never editing a contract test's assertion to make it pass.

skills.name: aid-orchestrate
skills.description: The orchestration rules for the root agent of the Think / Make / Learn workflow. The root holds the judgement, the user conversation, and the PRD approval gate, moves between the loops as the conversation calls for them, and delegates research, building, and review to the aid-* specialist roster. Use it at the start of any development work, when a long session needs re-anchoring, and whenever you're unsure whether to do something yourself or delegate it.

skills.name: aid-prd
skills.description: The PRD contract. A PRD is a living, user-owned document describing a feature as if it were finished now. Use it whenever you create, read, update, split, or check a PRD; when code and a PRD disagree; when a question of scope or behaviour comes up (the PRD is the first reference); or before proposing any edit to a document under docs/PRDs.

skills.name: aid-state
skills.description: How to drive the state record of the aid tool: the notes, follow-ups, deferred findings, and questions that aren't tasks in the graph but must be followed to the end of a piece of Make work. Covers the state.json format, the item kinds, the commands and their flags, when to record an item, how each is resolved to a durable home, and the finish check. Use it whenever something is noticed during Make that isn't a task, and when closing the work out.

skills.name: aid-think
skills.description: The Think loop, a judgement engine that cycles Explore, Challenge, Clarify, Choose and turns an unclear situation into user decisions recorded as PRD changes. Use it when the user wants to work through a feature, PRD, design question, or conflicting set of plans, branches, and references; asks you to pick their brain, go through questions, challenge them, or highlight conflicts between their ideas and the facts; or needs a clean set of PRD updates out of a messy situation.

skills.name: aid-think-challenge

skills.name: aid-think-choose

skills.name: aid-think-clarify
skills.description: The Clarify stage of the Think loop, loaded by aid-think and not an entry point. Gets the decisions only the user can make by asking one question at a time, each with context, evidence, options, and a recommendation, and waiting for the answer before the next.

skills.name: aid-think-explore
